title: Electron microscopy for virus identification and virus assemblage characterization
author: Kenneth M. Stedman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.eahbab6
materials: 0.2 µm filtered and centrifuged cell-free supernatant

steps.title: Spot sample onto EM grid
steps.instruction: Apply 5 µL of enrichment culture, or 0.2 µm‑filtered and centrifuged (10 min at 3000 g) cell‑free supernatant, onto carbon/formvar‑coated electron‑microscope grids (Ted Pella or EM Sciences).

steps.title: Allow sample absorption
steps.instruction: Let the sample absorb on the grid for 2 min.

steps.title: Wick, stain, and dry grid
steps.instruction: Remove excess liquid, stain, and dry the grid before imaging.

substeps.instruction: Remove sample from the grid by gently placing a ~1 cm² piece of filter paper perpendicular to the grid side; the liquid wicks away.
Place the grid on a 5 µL drop of 2 % Uranyl Acetate (or Phosphotungstate) and incubate for 15–30 s.
Remove the stain by wicking with fresh filter paper as above.
Air‑dry the grid for at least 10 min.

steps.title: Examine grid by TEM
steps.instruction: Image the prepared grids using transmission electron microscopy (e.g., JEOL 100 cx) operated at 100 keV; virus‑like particles are visible at 16,000–20,000× magnification.
